role_in_parent: Covers the final missing residue class modulo 8, completing the repaired case split.
statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p > 5 and p ≡ 7 (mod 8). For each k in {1,2,...,p-1}, let I(k) be the unique integer in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and define S = { k in {1,2,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| >= floor(p/4).

domain_restrictions: k ∈ {1,2,...,p-1} (hence gcd(k,p)=1, so inverse exists and is unique in 1..p-1)
S ⊆ {1,2,...,p-2} (k stops at p-2 so that k+1 ≤ p-1 and I(k+1) defined)
Comparisons I(k+1) < I(k) are standard integer comparisons on representatives 1..p-1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: ∀p ∈ Z (p prime, p>5, p ≡ 7 (mod 8)): define I_p:{1,...,p-1}→{1,...,p-1} by I_p(k) ≡ k^{-1} (mod p) (the unique r∈{1,...,p-1} with k·r ≡ 1 (mod p)). Let S_p = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I_p(k+1) < I_p(k) }. Then |S_p| ≥ ⌊p/4⌋.
quantifier_order: For all p: p is an integer, p is prime, p > 5, and p ≡ 7 (mod 8)
For each such p, for each k ∈ {1,...,p-1} define I(k) as the (unique) multiplicative inverse of k modulo p
For that p, define S = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }
Claim: |S| ≥ floor(p/4) (an inequality about the cardinality of S depending on p)

variables.name: p
variables.role: parameter: prime modulus with constraints p > 5 and p ≡ 7 (mod 8)

variables.name: k
variables.role: index variable ranging over residues mod p represented in 1..p-1

variables.name: I
variables.role: multiplicative inverse mod p: for each k, I(k) is the unique element of 1..p-1 with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)

variables.name: S
variables.role: indices k with strictly decreasing inverses: S = { k ∈ {1,..,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }

witness_dependencies: I(k) depends on both p and k (I = I_p); uniqueness of I(k) relies on p prime (gcd(k,p)=1)
S depends on p through I (S = S_p)
The lower bound floor(p/4) depends only on p (no hidden additional existential witnesses)
